title: SlateOne co-sell pipeline playbook
summary: Partner co-selling playbook for three target accounts, alignment on technical gating (VPC/private vs hosted), risk triage for key deals, ask list for security docs and joint collateral. Agreed pilot approach for one anchor account and timeline to enable joint outreach.
next_steps: Redwood to send tailored one-pager + joint email template by Thu 2026-04-02
SlateOne to provide account mapping and intro list by Mon 2026-04-06
Ethan to run quick compat checklist and share capability matrix by Fri 2026-04-03
action_items: Maya: draft joint outreach sequence and pricing bullets - due 2026-04-02
Priya: share final list of target 10 accounts and buyer contacts - due 2026-04-06
Ethan: produce short tech compatibility note (VPC, KMS, latency targets) - due 2026-04-03
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 16:00 PDT | Duration ~52 minutes | Attendees: Maya A., Ethan P., Renee C., Tom B., Ari K.; SlateOne: Jonas R., Priya M., Liam C.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood alliances team. We have Ethan our SE, and Renee from partnerships, and then SlateOne team — Jonas, Priya, Liam, nice to meet you.
00:14 - Jonas: Hi, thanks, Maya. Happy to be here, hope we can make this a pretty tactical session.
00:21 - Priya: Yep, quick agenda — walk through the deals we want to co-sell, technical gating, and then create a repeatable playbook.
00:30 - Maya: Perfect. Real quick, objective: identify three anchor opportunities we can jointly go after within 60 days, agree pilot mechanics, and list the security artifacts you need.
00:45 - Ethan: I'll also surface anything on the infra side that might block quick starts — e.g., whether they want Redwood Private or Hosted with VPC peering.
00:55 - Priya: Good. So first deal is with Beacon Med — payer analytics, big data residency asks. Second is Hytel Retail — latency-sensitive conversational agents. Third is NovaQ Labs — R&D platform, more flexible.
01:15 - Maya: Got it. Which of those is highest priority?
01:18 - Priya: Beacon is top because SlateOne already has an MSP relationship and initial intro. Beacon requires data residency in US-EAST and SOC2 plus enterprise SSO.
01:28 - Jonas: Also procurement timing — Beacon wants procurement in 6-8 weeks.
01:33 - Maya: Ok that's tight but doable. Let's map gating items. For Beacon: we need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML integration guide, data residency proof and optionally an on-prem/private deployment option. Ethan, high level — can we support that quickly?
01:46 - Ethan: Yes, from a product standpoint we have Hosted with region pinning and Dedicated pools. For strict data residency and customer-managed keys they'd typically want Redwood Private in a VPC or on-prem. That takes more time — packaging and infra agreements, but we can offer a bridge: dedicated capacity in a region plus encrypted-at-rest with KMS. It's mostly contractual.
02:07 - Liam: Quick question — what about live KV cache behavior for long conversations? We need assurance that the cache isn't shared across tenants.
02:16 - Ethan: Good call — KV cache and prefix caching are tenant-isolated. I'll add a short note to the tech sheet.
02:22 - Priya: Awesome. For Hytel Retail — they care about 50ms token latency target on checkout experiences. How realistic is that?
02:31 - Ethan: 50ms per token is aggressive. Depends on model size and local region. With smaller quantized models and dedicated GPUs you can get close for shorter sequences, but for 1k-context it will be higher. We can propose a hybrid — routing by latency policy: critical paths on dedicated low-latency pools, bulk async on lower-cost variants.
02:56 - Jonas: Do you have benchmark artifacts we can share with Hytel? They want token-level cost and latency breakdowns to justify the spend.
03:05 - Maya: Yes, we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet. Action item: Maya to attach 'latency-cost-bench-2026Q1.xlsx' to the follow-up email.
03:14 - Priya: Great. On NovaQ, they have an internal ML team and are more flexible; they'd want to co-design an eval set. Could we support joint evals?
03:23 - Ethan: Absolutely. We can offer eval harness access and run initial regressions with their prompt set. That typically takes one week for an initial pass.
03:32 - Maya: Let's talk risk triage. Which deals are procurement-heavy versus technical-heavy?
03:36 - Priya: Beacon - procurement & security; Hytel - latency/cost; NovaQ - technical evaluation and custom embeddings.
03:44 - Tom: On the security ask — SOC2 and ISO documents we can share via the partner portal PDF link. For KMS/HSM we have integrations listed with major cloud KMS providers; for on-prem we have an optional connector package.
03:56 - Jonas: Will you be able to sign an NDA / DPA quickly for Beacon? They asked for dual-sig.
04:02 - Maya: Yes we've got a partner DPA template. I'll loop legal but we can push a draft within 3 business days.
04:08 - Jonas: Perfect.

04:20 - [20: second block — deeper technical dive — timestamps approximate]
04:20 - Ethan: I want to call out one technical nuance — when we talk about private deployments (Redwood Private), the control plane remains on our side unless it's the on-prem distribution. For highly regulated customers that insist on air-gapped, we do an on-prem package; otherwise VPC + customer-managed keys is usually sufficient.
04:42 - Liam: That distinction was unclear in the earlier doc SlateOne saw. Good to clarify. Does the hosted API ever store ephemeral artifacts in our logs?
04:52 - Tom: By default we have configurable retention. For enterprise deals we can turn off retention and have audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM. We'll add a note.
05:03 - Priya: On pricing — what's the playbook? We want price anchors to present to buyers — subscription for dedicated + per-token overage? Bundled pilots?
05:13 - Maya: Typical co-sell structure: joint proposal with reserved committed capacity (monthly) + usage tiers. For pilots we do time-limited free credits or a trial committed minimum to offset provisioning. We'll propose a three-month pilot with a capped spend; SlateOne to handle initial intro and we co-bill or do a referral fee depending on procurement.
05:32 - Jonas: Referral fee conversation — we want clarity on margins and credit splits early.
05:37 - Renee: From partnerships side, SlateOne referral deals default to a 10% referral fee on net new revenue for first 12 months unless we have an SPA for revenue share. We can be flexible for anchor accounts.
05:50 - Maya: Let's not get bogged down now — we'll include a clear referral fee note in the joint one-pager.
05:58 - Priya: Sounds good.

06:10 - [approx 06:10 — recording jumps a little — transcription artifacts]
06:10 - Ethan: Technical checklist I propose we use: 1) Data residency requirement, 2) Auth method (SSO/SAML/OAuth), 3) KMS needed, 4) expected QPS and latency SLO, 5) required retention/audit logs, 6) model/regulation constraints. I'll share as a Google sheet.
06:34 - Priya: That'll be helpful. For Beacon procurement, they will demand vendor security questionnaire — do you have a standard security package?
06:42 - Tom: Yes, link to security pack in partner portal. We also have a short slide deck summarizing isolation and encryption practices.
06:51 - Jonas: Who runs the technical call with Beacon? SlateOne wants to speak to an SE.
06:55 - Maya: Ethan will own that. Proposed slot next Wed 2026-04-07.
07:02 - Ethan: Works for me; I'll prep a short demo of dedicated capacity and show autoscale behaviors.
07:10 - Priya: For Hytel, can we do a micro-benchmark? Measure end-to-end latency for their checkout flow?
07:17 - Ethan: Yes — ideally we replicate their sequence lengths and test in the same region. We can do a run in under a week if they provide prompt traces.
07:26 - Priya: We'll pull that.

07:35 - [mid-call — questions and objections]
07:35 - Jonas: A couple of pushbacks we've heard from customers: vendor lock-in concerns, and cost unpredictability with tokenized billing.
07:44 - Maya: On lock-in, we emphasize standard model artifacts, exportable fine-tuned weights where applicable, and routing policies that let customers failover to open-source variants. On cost, Redwood Optimize provides suggested batching and quantization profiles to bound spend; we can show a before/after example in the benchmark.
07:59 - Liam: For compliance-heavy buyers, how invasive is the on-prem option in terms of maintenance overhead?
08:06 - Tom: On-prem requires an ops handover; we offer an install bundle and a 90-day managed runbook where Redwood supports the initial run. After that it's handed to customer ops. We can discuss managed support as an add-on.
08:20 - Priya: Okay. Can we get an SOC2 summary and also a quick note on data deletion procedures?
08:28 - Maya: Yes, I'll include both in the follow-up.

08:35 - [deeper strategy — outreach cadence]
08:35 - Renee: For the playbook outreach, I recommend a three-touch sequence: 1) intro email co-signed by Jonas + Maya with one-pager and benchmark highlights, 2) personalized value email mapping to buyer persona, 3) invitation to technical working session. We can A/B test subject lines.
08:53 - Priya: We'll own the first intro but want Redwood content.
08:56 - Maya: We'll provide: 1) one-pager, 2) joint email template, 3) benchmark spreadsheet, 4) demo invite calendar link.
09:06 - Jonas: For Beacon, can we co-host a 30-minute exec briefing with procurement and security?
09:12 - Maya: Yes — we'll prep a 15-minute SLIDES deck for execs and 30-minute for technical teams.
09:18 - Priya: Who will lead the technical deep-dive?
09:20 - Ethan: I'll lead the SE session; Tom will back me up on security.

09:28 - [noise / slight crosstalk, transcription artifacts — words sometimes merged]
09:28 - Priya: One more ask — SlateOne would like a short training for sales on how to position Redwood value prop. Could be 30 minutes.
09:36 - Maya: Absolutely. We can do a partner enablement session — 30 min, deck and two example objection responses.
09:44 - Renee: And a shared playbook doc where we track leads and statuses; is there a partner portal or do you prefer a shared CRM?
09:51 - Maya: We can do either. For now let's use a shared spreadsheet and we can sync with your SFDC later.
09:58 - Priya: Great.

10:04 - [last 10 minutes — recap and commitments]
10:04 - Maya: Quick recap: Action items — Maya send one-pager + joint email + benchmark by Thu 2026-04-02; Ethan produce tech checklist and capability notes by Fri 2026-04-03; Priya/SlateOne to share account list by Mon 2026-04-06; schedule Beacon intro + SE call for Wed 2026-04-07. Any objections?
10:26 - Jonas: Sounds good. Two items — please include a pricing anchor for a three-month pilot and the referral fee language.
10:34 - Maya: Will do.
10:36 - Priya: Also ask that all artifacts be uploaded to the partner folder so sales can access.
10:40 - Maya: We'll put everything in the shared drive and send links.
10:44 - Liam: Small tech question — for Hytel's latency test can you capture p95 and p99 as well as average?
10:50 - Ethan: Yep, will include p50/p95/p99 and token cost breakdown.
10:55 - Priya: Thanks everyone. Any final words?
10:57 - Renee: Thanks — excited to move.
11:00 - Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the attachments.

11:10 - [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional merge of names (e.g., Redwood Private sometimes shown as red wood privet), small typos, and timestamps approximate. References: benchmark spreadsheet, partner portal links, security pack PDF, joint one-pager.

End of transcript.
